observations: User Connected App flow stores per-user token cache, validates OAuth state and refreshes expired tokens.
get_backend_app_token uses a userless token cache plus OAuth2 BackendApplicationClient/client-credentials flow and reuses a non-expired cached token.
The DocType also exposes provider discovery/introspection/userinfo/revocation configuration fields.
Webhook can bind document lifecycle events and evaluate a safe_eval condition.
Dynamic URLs and JSON bodies can be rendered from templates; custom headers and POST/PUT/DELETE are configurable.
Optional HMAC signing is supported and delivery retries/logging are implemented in-process.

behavior: A reserved tenant/app service principal acquires client_credentials tokens without a browser flow.
Backend tokens use the same AES-GCM identity binding, encrypted D1 cache, version CAS and acquisition lease as user refresh.
Webhook service_account credentials resolve only from trusted tenant runtime bindings and never from request payload.
Document subscriptions select committed domain events by bounded event pattern and static mapping.
Dynamic Frappe condition/template/URL/method/header fields fail closed instead of being silently interpreted.
Targets are operator-allowlisted HTTPS, payload snapshots are immutable, delivery is durable with fenced retries/dead-letter/attributed replay.

intentional_differences: Forge does not execute Frappe safe_eval/Jinja webhook conditions, dynamic URLs or arbitrary request methods/headers; fixed JSON POST plus static mapping and trusted credentials is the deliberate security contract.

Provider discovery/introspection/userinfo/revocation endpoints are not accepted as browser-controlled runtime expansion. Provider endpoints/hosts are operator-pinned and disconnect is a local encrypted-cache tombstone.

No upstream runtime oracle is used to claim identical provider behavior. Backend client-credentials is implemented from the pinned source contract, while the residual flexibility is closed only as an intentional difference.
closure_claim: backend OAuth semantics implemented; remaining integration flexibility intentionally narrower and fail-closed
